high.title: VN-Index regains 1,800 points, but many investors still unhappy
high.summary: The VN-Index closed 25 points higher (+1.41%) at 1,800.65 points on April 15, surpassing the psychologically important 1,800 level despite profit-taking pressure in the afternoon. HoSE trading volume reached 910.7 million shares worth over 24,431 billion VND. The VN30 basket gained 15.05 points to 1,961.60 points. Vingroup stocks led the rally with VIC hitting ceiling price (+6.9%), contributing 18.75 points to the index, while VHM added 7.04 points. For FX traders, this equity market strength may support the VND by attracting capital flows, though sustained foreign selling remains a concern for both equities and currency stability.

high.title: Experts: VN-Index's 2,000-point target still has basis for expectation
high.summary: Vietcombank Fund Management's portfolio director identified three key market factors: interest rates, inflation, and capital flows. Vietnam's interest rate environment has risen significantly since late 2025, with deposit rates climbing from 5-6% to 7-8%, making deposits more attractive versus risky assets like equities. This stems from high credit growth outpacing deposit mobilization, forcing banks to raise rates to balance funding and meet safety ratios. For bond investors, this suggests continued upward pressure on yields as banks compete for deposits. The rising rate environment creates headwinds for both equity markets and government bond prices.

high.title: A force "sold" nearly 40,000 billion VND of Vietnamese stocks since the beginning of the year, what is happening?
high.summary: Foreign investors continued their selling spree, offloading nearly 40,000 billion VND worth of Vietnamese stocks in just over 4 months of 2026, despite the market upgrade news. VCBF's fund manager explained this reflects global capital flows shifting back to the US as higher US interest rates make domestic investments more attractive than overseas allocations. When comparing to markets like Vietnam, investors also face FX risk, significantly reducing relative attractiveness. This massive capital outflow creates sustained pressure on both the VND/USD exchange rate and Vietnamese government bond yields, as foreign selling reduces demand for VND-denominated assets.

medium.title: MASVN: There is basis to assume that VN-Index has bottomed
medium.summary: Mirae Asset notes similarities with April 2025 when Trump announced negotiation delays after US 10-year Treasury yields exceeded 4.3%. Markets typically bottom when uncertainty peaks and signals shift from "escalation" to "negotiation." The March 23 announcement to delay Iran strikes mirrors the April 2025 market bottom pattern.

medium.title: DSC CEO: VN-Index corrections if they occur could be very "deep and painful"
medium.summary: DSC's CEO projects VN-Index could reach 1,950-2,000 points in positive scenarios with 10% GDP growth, reduced US-Iran tensions, and stable energy prices. Support comes from 10-15% earnings growth and attractive P/E of 11x, plus potential 5-8 billion USD from market upgrade. However, warns of risks from prolonged geopolitical tensions, inflation pressure, and high interest rates and exchange rates.

medium.title: 6 banks plan to spend nearly 34,000 billion VND in cash dividends: Not VPBank or MB, this is the bank spending most for shareholders
medium.summary: LPBank leads with nearly 9,000 billion VND cash dividend (30% ratio), VPBank plans 4,000 billion (5%), and MB targets 1,840 billion (8%). These large dividend payouts may impact bank liquidity and interbank rates as banks distribute significant cash to shareholders.

medium.title: Securities company Q1/2026 update: First hundred-billion loss appears
medium.summary: EVS Securities reported massive losses as operating revenue plunged 91% to 8 billion VND while operating costs soared to 188 billion VND. FVTPL gains collapsed from 75 billion to 2 billion VND, and brokerage revenue halved. This reflects broader challenges in the securities industry amid market volatility.
